title: SLO trigger simulator and policy suggestor for adaptive rollout safeguards
creator: Ariadne Patel
description: Build a traffic-driven SLO trigger simulator and a policy suggestor that recommends adaptive rollback thresholds and schedule windows for canary, A/B, and shadow traffic rollouts. The simulator will synthesize realistic mixes of traffic (latency distributions, error bursts, token consumption, throughput spikes) across user cohorts and load patterns to evaluate false positive and false negative rates of candidate rollback triggers. The policy suggestor will output tunable threshold sets (per-cohort and global), hysteresis parameters, and cost bounds, and expose a compact policy JSON consumed by the rollout controller. This ticket covers design, simulator prototype, evaluation harness, and integration spec for the rollout controller API.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can synthesize traffic with configurable percentile latency distributions, error-rate burstiness, token-per-request distributions, and throughput ramps
Policy suggestor outputs a ranked set of threshold candidates (latency p95/p99, error rate, token cost per 1k requests, throughput drop) with estimated FP/FN rates and expected cost impact
Simulator produces ROC-like curves and hysteresis simulation traces for each candidate policy over 50 randomized seeds
End-to-end test: rollout controller consumes policy JSON and executes simulated canary run; rollback decision observed matches simulator prediction within +/-5% on trigger rate
Integration tests and evaluation notebooks are checked into internal repo and linkable from this ticket
Documentation: design doc and operator guide describing how to read/accept suggested policies and safe defaults for P0 customers
implementation_notes: Simulator will be implemented in Python with a fast event-driven core and a lightweight Go shim for the rollout-controller integration tests
Traffic model: mixture of log-normal latency kernels, Poisson and bursty on-off error generators, and empirically-derived token-per-request distributions from production traces (anonymized)
Policy scoring: compute precision/recall and cost delta per-threshold; introduce a cost-bounded objective to prefer policies that limit token-cost regressions
Cohorts: support sticky-user cohorts and request-path cohorts; allow per-cohort weight overrides to simulate skewed traffic during staged rollouts
Hysteresis: support configurable cool-down windows, escalate-on-repeated-failure and decay-based thresholds to reduce flapping
Output: JSON policy bundle schema v1 that includes signals, thresholds, hysteresis params, recommended schedule (initial fraction, ramp cadence, min-observation window)
Integration: rollout-controller consumes policy bundle via admin endpoint and records simulated decision traces to Grafana for analysis
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: synthetic traffic may not capture rare real-world failure modes -> Mitigation: seed simulator with anonymized production tail samples and add manual failure-case injection
Risk: overfitting suggestor to training seeds -> Mitigation: require cross-seed validation and report variance bands on recommendations

Risk: suggested thresholds may be too conservative and increase time-to-rollout -> Mitigation: include cost-aware scoring to balance safety vs. rollout velocity and provide a 'recommended' and 'safe' tier
Risk: operator confusion about policy fields -> Mitigation: ship operator guide with examples and visualization tools in the Console
test_plan: Unit tests for signal generators (latency, error burst, token distribution)
End-to-end smoke test: policy bundle applied to local rollout-controller and decision trace validated
Benchmark: simulator can run 10k simulated requests/sec on a standard CI worker for parameter sweeps
Manual review: PM + SRE sign-off on default safe policy before rollout to production canary workflows
